We define a quasilocal mass of Bartnik type, and establish its positivity and temporal monotonicity properties for two classes of domains associated with black holes. More precisely, we first show that the quasilocal mass is strictly positive for spacelike hypersurfaces that are: compact with apparent horizon boundary or noncompact with asymptotically flat ends and containing an apparent horizon in any admissible extension. Secondly, we show that the quasilocal mass is monotonically nondecreasing in time within evolutionary scenarios related to the two aforementioned settings.

## Abstract

The Minkowski measurability of self-similar sets is closely linked to the lattice or non-lattice nature of the contraction ratios of the underlying iterated function system. A long-standing conjecture of Lapidus asserts that under certain conditions a self-similar fractal set is not Minkowski measurable if and only if it is of lattice-type. While the conjecture has been confirmed for self-similar subsets of $\mathbb{R}$, the lattice case remains open in general in higher dimensions. This paper establishes non-Minkowski measurability for a class of regular n-flake dusts in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2}$. This condition depends only on the logarithms of the contraction ratios and is therefore easy to verify, making it particularly appealing as a potential characterization.

The non-lattice case is by now well understood: Gatzouras [2] showed that self-similar sets in ${\mathbb{R}}^{d}$ satisfying the OSC are Minkowski measurable whenever the associated IFS is non-lattice. In contrast, the lattice case presents significantly greater difficulties. In dimension one, the conjecture has been completely resolved through the work of several authors, culminating in a full characterization of Minkowski measurability for self-similar subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ [3,4]. However, for dimensions $d\ge 2$, the situation remains far from settled, and a complete understanding is still lacking. We refer to [5] for a comprehensive overview of the current state of the art.

In higher dimensions, available results typically require additional structural assumptions. One prominent example is the pluriphase condition, which yields non-Minkowski measurability for certain lattice self-similar sets under suitable hypotheses [6]. This approach, as well as several related results, is based on renewal-theoretic methods and the analysis of scaling functions associated with the parallel volume. Another line of research focuses on exact tube formulas and employs techniques from the theory of complex dimensions and fractal zeta functions. While this framework has proven to be very powerful and has led to deep insights, it often involves technically demanding computations and is not always easily applicable to concrete families of sets.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate the Minkowski measurability of a class of self-similar sets in ${\mathbb{R}}^{2}$, namely the so-called n-flake dusts. These sets form families of lattice self-similar sets satisfying the open set condition, and thus provide a suitable testing ground for the conjectured relationship between lattice structure and non-measurability.

Our main result shows that, under a geometric condition on the contraction ratio, n-flake dusts fail to be Minkowski measurable. The proof is based on a detailed analysis of the volume of parallel sets and exploits the presence of hole points, a notion introduced in Section 2.5, which induce a lack of smoothness in the associated volume function. More precisely, we show that the function $\epsilon \mapsto {\lambda }^{2}\left({F}_{\epsilon }\right)$ is not twice differentiable at a critical scale, which implies that the corresponding normalized volume function cannot be constant. This approach provides a new mechanism for establishing non-Minkowski measurability in the lattice case and thus contribute further evidence toward the conjectured characterization of Minkowski measurability beyond one dimension.

The paper is organized as follows. Section 2 contains the required preliminaries (see Section 2.1, Section 2.2, Section 2.3, Section 2.4 and Section 2.5) together with a brief overview of known results (see Section 2.6). In Section 3, we introduce the class of n-flake dusts and discuss their relation to the general framework. Section 4 is devoted to the proof of the main result on Minkowski non-measurability of n-flake dusts.

For lattice self-similar boundaries such as the Koch curve, which we show fail LTB (the accumulated turn on any subarc being infinite by self-similarity), existing results on the failure of Minkowski measurability establish, rigorously and unconditionally, that the continuous tube volume of such a boundary oscillates persistently under refinement, with no stabilizing rate.
For LTB boundaries (in particular smooth or par(r)-regular curves) the collapse follows a well-defined power law, quantitatively analogous to the classical curse of dimensionality; we establish this regime unconditionally. For lattice self-similar boundaries such as the Koch curve, which we show fail LTB (the accumulated turn on any subarc being infinite by self-similarity), existing results on the failure of Minkowski measurability establish, rigorously and unconditionally, that the continuous tube volume of such a boundary oscillates persistently under refinement, with no stabilizing rate. We give a partial, independent argument a renewal relation together with a segment-phase mechanism– that the discrete grid box-counting analogue used in digitization inherits this oscillatory behavior, but completing this argument reduces to an open combinatorial question about how self-similar boundary segments tile a reference grid. Direct numerical experiments on both the open Koch curve and the closed Koch snowflake, across several octaves of refinement, are inconclusive on this specific point: the measured oscillation amplitude decreases rather than stabilizes over the range of resolutions we could feasibly compute, consistent with either a small non-zero asymptotic floor or with eventual convergence. Conditional on this combinatorial question being resolved in the affirmative, digitization of lattice self-similar boundaries would be categorically more severe than the LTB case, and provably not resolution-stable: no schedule of refinement would yield a digitized representation converging to a fixed structure, regardless of the estimator applied to it. To isolate this mechanism we introduce a minimal Gedankenexperiment distinguishing the digitized boundary layer from the subset actually visited by a scanning process, and reconstruct it for both regimes. The analysis separates what is established unconditionally (the vanishing of relative boundary accessibility under digitization) from what remains conditional on an explicitly identified, still-open combinatorial question– the categorically pathological character of the rate at which that vanishing occurs.

#### Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem

Michiyuki Watanabe

We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $\alpha > 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-\alpha^2,0)$.
